'''Gaston Maurice Julia''' (3 February 1893 – 19 March 1978) was a French mathematician who devised the formula for the [[Julia set]]. His works were popularized by [[Benoit Mandelbrot]]; the Julia and Mandelbrot [[fractal]]s are closely related. He founded, independently with [[Pierre Fatou]], the modern theory of [[holomorphic dynamics]].

==Military service==
Julia was born in the [[Algeria]]n town of [[Sidi Bel Abbès]], at the time governed by the [[French Algeria|French]]. During his youth, he had an interest in mathematics and music. His studies were interrupted at the age of 21, when France became involved in [[World War I]] and Julia was conscripted to serve with the army. During an attack he suffered a severe injury, losing his nose. His many operations to remedy the situation were all unsuccessful, and for the rest of his life he resigned himself to wearing a leather strap around the area where his nose had been.

==Career in mathematics==
Julia gained attention for his mathematical work at the age of 25, in 1918, when his 199-page ''Mémoire sur l'itération des fonctions rationnelles'' ("Memoir on the Iteration of Rational Functions") was featured in the ''[[Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées]]''.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Julia, Gaston|author-link=Gaston Julia|title=Mémoire sur l'itération des fonctions rationnelles|journal=[[Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées]]|year=1918|volume=1|pages=47–245|language=fr|url=http://sites.mathdoc.fr/JMPA/PDF/JMPA_1918_8_1_A2_0.pdf}}</ref> This article gained immense popularity among mathematicians and earned him the ''Grand Prix des Sciences Mathématiques'' of the [[French Academy of Sciences]] in 1918. But after this brief moment of fame, his works were mostly forgotten<ref>Ari Ben-Menahem: ''Historical Encyclopedia of Natural and Mathematical Sciences'', Springer, {{ISBN|978-3-540-68832-7}}, p. 3427</ref> until [[Benoit Mandelbrot]] mentioned them in his works on [[fractal]]s in the French book ''Les Objets Fractals: Forme, Hasard et Dimension'', later translated in 1977 as ''Fractals: Form, Chance and Dimension''.<ref>''Fractals: Form, Chance and Dimension'', by Benoît Mandelbrot; W H Freeman and Co, 1977; {{isbn|0-7167-0473-0}}</ref>

[[File:Julia set (highres 01).jpg|thumb|Example of a Julia set (C = [0.285, 0.01])]]

On 19 March 1978, Julia died in Paris at the age of 85.

Julia was also father to [[Marc Julia]],<ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1002/anie.201006207 | title=Marc Julia (1922–2010) | year=2010 | last1=Chottard | first1=Jean-Claude | last2=Lallemand | first2=Jean-Yves | last3=Mansuy | first3=Daniel | last4=Verpeaux | first4=Jean-Noël | journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition | volume=49 | issue=48 | pages=9038–9039 | doi-access=free }}</ref> the French organic chemist who invented the [[Julia olefination]].

==World War II and collaboration==

Julia [[Collaboration with Nazi Germany and Fascist Italy|collaborated]] with [[Nazi Germany]] during the [[occupation of France]]; recruiting French mathematicians to collaborate with the [[ZbMATH Open|Zentralblatt für Mathematik]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Audin, Michèle|title=Publier sous l'Occupation I. Autour du cas de Jacques Feldbau et de l'Académie des sciences|journal=Revue d'Histoire des Mathématiques|year=2009|volume=15|pages=27|language=fr|url=https://sgm.hypotheses.org/files/2017/11/RHM_2009__15_1_7_0.pdf}}</ref> He was suspended for a few weeks after the [[liberation of France]],<ref>{{cite book |last=Singer |first=Claude |title=L'université libérée, l'université épurée, 1943-1947 |trans-title=Liberated university, purged university, 1943-1947 |year=1997 |pages=283 |language=fr |isbn=9782251380377 |oclc=797449151 |publisher=Belles Lettres |url=https://www.decitre.fr/livres/l-universite-liberee-l-universite-epuree-1943-1947-9782251380377.html}}</ref> but according to [[Michèle Audin]]:<ref>{{cite book |last=Audin |first=Michèle |title=Fatou, Julia, Montel |series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics |year=2009 |volume=2014 |pages=179 |language=fr |isbn=978-3-642-17854-2 |oclc=964823520 |doi=10.1007/978-3-642-17854-2 |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-642-17854-2}}</ref> {{Blockquote|This was followed by no sanction, as the epuration committee was (unanimously...) too impressed by his status of "{{lang|fr|italic=no|[[Gueules cassées|gueule cassée]]}}" to do anything. Then he resumed his normal activities, professor at the Sorbonne and l'Ecole Polytechnique, was president of the Académie des Sciences in 1950, etc.}}
